# ISA — Ideal State Artifact

The ISA is the single document that articulates "done" for any thing whose ideal state we are pursuing — a project, an application, a library, infrastructure, a work session, an art piece, a strategic decision. It serves five identities simultaneously: ideal state articulation, test harness, build verification, done condition, system of record.

This skill owns the canonical template, the workflows that generate and refine ISAs, and the example library.

---

## The Twelve-Section Body (locked v6.2.0)

Every ISA may have up to twelve body sections. The tier completeness gate decides which are required at which effort tier; sections never appear empty. **Order is fixed**.

| # | Section | Purpose | Written At |
|---|---------|---------|------------|
| 1 | `## Problem` | What is broken or missing right now that makes the ideal state worth pursuing | OBSERVE |
| 2 | `## Vision` | What euphoric surprise looks like — experiential intent, 1–5 sentences | OBSERVE |
| 3 | `## Out of Scope` | Anti-vision — what is *not* included in this ideal state, declared upfront in prose | OBSERVE |
| 4 | `## Principles` | Substrate-independent truths (Deutsch reach) the work must respect | OBSERVE |
| 5 | `## Constraints` | Immovable architectural mandates that bound the solution space | OBSERVE |
| 6 | `## Goal` | The hard-to-vary spine — 1–3 sentences naming verifiable done | OBSERVE |
| 7 | `## Criteria` | Atomic ISCs (Ideal State Criteria) — one binary tool probe each, including derived `Anti:` ISCs | OBSERVE → EXECUTE |
| 8 | `## Test Strategy` | Per-ISC verification approach — `isc | type | check | threshold | tool` | OBSERVE/PLAN |
| 9 | `## Features` | Work breakdown — `name | description | satisfies: [ISC-N…] | depends_on: [feature…] | parallelizable: bool` | PLAN |
| 10 | `## Decisions` | Timestamped decision log including dead ends; `refined:` prefix for Goal/ISC restructures | any phase |
| 11 | `## Changelog` | Conjecture / refuted-by / learned / criterion-now entries — Deutsch error-correction trail | LEARN |
| 12 | `## Verification` | Evidence that each ISC passed — quoted command output, file content, screenshot path | VERIFY |

---

## Three-Guardrail Taxonomy (Principles vs Constraints vs Anti-criteria)

Adjacent concepts. Distinguished by **who they bind**.

| Guardrail | Binds | Tone | Example | Lives In |
|-----------|-------|------|---------|----------|
| **Principles** | The *thinking* | Aspirational, generalizable | "User-facing systems prioritize responsiveness." | `## Principles` |
| **Constraints** | The *solution space* | Immovable, non-negotiable | "We do not roll our own cryptography — OAuth via industry-standard libraries only." | `## Constraints` |
| **Out of Scope** | The *vision* | Declared, explicit, prose | "Mobile native apps are not part of v1." | `## Out of Scope` |
| **Anti-criteria** | The *test surface* | Granular, testable, yes/no | "Anti: /admin returns 200 in v1 build." | `## Criteria` (with `Anti:` prefix) |

The first three are author-stated (declarative). Anti-criteria are derived — they are how Out of Scope, Constraints, and Principles become probe-able.

---

## Tier Completeness Gate (HARD at all tiers)

Mirrors the v6.1.0 thinking-floor non-relaxability. Required sections per tier:

| Tier | Required Sections |
|------|-------------------|
| **E1** | Goal, Criteria |
| **E2** | Problem, Goal, Criteria, Test Strategy |
| **E3** | Problem, Vision, Out of Scope, Constraints, Goal, Criteria, Features, Test Strategy |
| **E4** | All twelve sections |
| **E5** | All twelve + active Interview workflow run before BUILD |

**Project ISA override:** any `<project>/ISA.md` requires E3+ structure regardless of the active task's tier. The project file is the long-lived source of truth; one transient E1 task must not downgrade it.

`CheckCompleteness` workflow enforces this gate. A miss blocks `phase: complete` until the missing sections are filled in.

---

## Workflow Routing

Match the verb in the request to a workflow. When ambiguous, default to Scaffold for new ISAs and CheckCompleteness for audits.

| Verb / Intent | Workflow | File |
|---------------|----------|------|
| "scaffold", "create", "generate", "new ISA from this prompt", "extract feature as ephemeral" | **Scaffold** | `Workflows/Scaffold.md` |
| "interview me", "fill in the ISA", "deepen", "ask me questions" | **Interview** | `Workflows/Interview.md` |
| "check", "audit", "score this ISA", "is it complete?" | **CheckCompleteness** | `Workflows/CheckCompleteness.md` |
| "reconcile", "merge feature file back", "ephemeral → master" | **Reconcile** | `Workflows/Reconcile.md` |
| "seed", "bootstrap from this repo", "draft an ISA from existing code" | **Seed** | `Workflows/Seed.md` |
| "append decision", "append changelog", "append verification", "record C/R/L entry" | **Append** | `Workflows/Append.md` |

**When executing a workflow, output this notification directly:**

```
Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **ISA** skill to ACTION...
```

---

## Gotchas

The highest-information-density part of this skill. Each entry captures a non-obvious failure mode that has bitten real ISA work.

- **ID-stability is the cornerstone of Reconcile — never re-number on edit.** When the Splitting Test produces a finer-grained version of `ISC-7`, preserve `ISC-7` as the parent and add `ISC-7.1`, `ISC-7.2`, etc. Even when an ISC is dropped, leave a tombstone (`- [ ] ISC-N: [DROPPED — see Decisions YYYY-MM-DD]`). Reconcile keys on stable IDs; renumbering breaks ephemeral feature-file merges silently and the failure mode looks like "the worker's checkmarks didn't land in master."
- **Ephemeral files are derived views, never sources of truth.** Scaffold's `--ephemeral` mode produces a slice of the master ISA at `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/_ephemeral/<feature>.md`. Workers operate against that slice; Reconcile merges back. Hand-editing master content from an ephemeral file is policy-forbidden — the master is what persists; the ephemeral is what gets archived.
- **The Changelog format is non-negotiable.** Every entry needs all four pieces (`conjectured`, `refuted by`, `learned`, `criterion now`) in that order. Append refuses to write a partial C/R/L; if any of the four is missing, the entry is a Decision, not a Changelog. The format is what makes the Deutsch error-correction trail auditable across sessions.
- **Project ISAs upgrade tier to `max(declared, E3)` regardless of the active task's tier.** A `<project>/ISA.md` is the long-lived system of record for a thing with persistent identity. One transient E1 task on the project must NOT downgrade the structural minimum. CheckCompleteness applies this override automatically.
- **Empty sections never appear.** The twelve-section body is a *capacity*, not a *requirement* at every tier. Sections required-but-empty for the tier are populated; sections not required and not yet written are simply absent from the file. CheckCompleteness distinguishes `present` / `thin` / `missing` / `empty` and only `empty` is acceptable for `Verification` before VERIFY phase.
- **Anti-criteria are derived from Out of Scope plus regression-prevention concerns.** They are how the prose-guardrails (Out of Scope, Constraints, Principles) become probe-able. At least one is required at every tier; the absence of an anti-criterion at OBSERVE is a hard CheckCompleteness failure.
- **Antecedents are required when the goal is experiential.** For art, design, content, and anything that has to "land," at least one ISC must use the `Antecedent:` prefix to name a precondition that reliably produces the target experience. Verifiable goals (build, deploy, schema) don't need antecedents; experiential goals always do.
- **Reconcile is deterministic — there are no conflicts to resolve.** Either an ISC ID exists in master (mechanical merge) or it doesn't (abort with ID-stability violation). If the ephemeral made structural changes (split ISC-7 into ISC-7.1/ISC-7.2), those structural changes belong in master via a separate Edit by the user *before* Reconcile runs.
- **The format spec wins on contradiction.** `IsaFormat.md` is the file-shape contract. If this skill's prose ever drifts from the format spec, the spec is canonical and the skill updates to match — not the reverse.

---

## Examples

The `Examples/` directory holds twelve reference ISAs spanning the tier (E1–E5) × domain (code / art / design / ops / marketplace / enterprise) matrix. Always start by reading the canonical showpiece before scaffolding a new ISA — copy its section headers, then populate. Pick the example closest to your domain + scale as a template.

**Showpiece**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Examples/canonical-isa.md` | **BeanLine** — peer-to-peer specialty-coffee marketplace. The showpiece reference, fully populated across all twelve sections with real-feeling Decisions and a four-piece C/R/L Changelog. Read this first. |

**Code**

| File | Tier | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `Examples/e1-minimal.md` | E1 | Add a `--no-color` flag to a CLI tool. <90s task, Goal + 4 ISCs only. Demonstrates the fast-path floor. |
| `Examples/e2-backup-verify.md` | E2 | Add SHA-256 verification to a backup CLI's `--verify` mode. Single-domain, 18 ISCs. |
| `Examples/e3-project.md` | E3 | Build an arxiv metadata extractor CLI. Mid-size project, 12 ISCs, eight sections. |
| `Examples/e4-api-migration.md` | E4 | Migrate a public API from REST to GraphQL with 6-month backwards-compat. Cross-cutting, 73 ISCs, all twelve sections. |
| `Examples/e5-desktop-app.md` | E5 | **WattWatch** — open-source desktop app for personal home-energy monitoring. Single-user app pattern, 50 ISCs, populated Changelog. |

**Art (experiential — antecedents required)**

| File | Tier | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `Examples/e3-essay.md` | E3 | Write a 1500-word essay on a specific thesis. Experiential goal, antecedent ISCs, post-publish reception probes. |
| `Examples/e5-album.md` | E5 | **Mariner Frequencies** — produce a 12-track instrumental album over 6 months. Long-form experiential, multi-act Changelog. |

**Design (experiential)**

| File | Tier | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `Examples/e3-help-redesign.md` | E3 | Redesign a CLI tool's `--help` output for first-encounter clarity. Antecedents + usability tests. |
| `Examples/e4-brand-identity.md` | E4 | **Cardinal** — brand identity for a small fintech startup (logo + type + color + voice + first 5 marketing surfaces). 56 ISCs, 6 antecedents. |

**Ops**

| File | Tier | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `Examples/e2-rotate-credential.md` | E2 | Rotate a production deploy credential in CI. Demonstrates the ISA primitive applied to ops/runbook work. 16 ISCs. |

**Enterprise**

| File | Tier | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `Examples/e5-enterprise.md` | E5 | **Beacon Health Alliance** — multi-region HIPAA-compliant patient portal for a 50-hospital network. Compliance anti-criteria, multi-team parallelizable features, 68 ISCs across all twelve sections. |

---

## ID Stability Rule

**ISC IDs never re-number on edit.** When the Splitting Test produces a finer-grained version of `ISC-7`, the original number is preserved as the parent and children become `ISC-7.1`, `ISC-7.2`, etc. Do not collapse the numbering even if the ISC is dropped — leave a tombstone marker so historical references in Decisions, Changelog, and Verification remain valid.

This rule exists because `Reconcile` is keyed on ISC IDs. If IDs renumber across edits, ephemeral feature-file reconciliation breaks silently. The renumbering ban is what makes feature-file workflows safe.

---

## Ephemeral Feature Files (Ralph Loop / Maestro pattern)

When a feature is to be worked in an isolated context (Ralph Loop, Maestro, parallel coding-agent instances), the Algorithm invokes:

```
Skill("ISA", "extract feature <name> as ephemeral file")
```

`Scaffold` (with `--ephemeral` mode) produces a derived view at `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/_ephemeral/<feature>.md` containing only the slice relevant to that feature: the Vision and Goal as read-only context, the relevant Constraints, the ISCs in the feature's `satisfies:` list with stable IDs, the matching Test Strategy entries, and an empty Verification section.

A fresh-context agent operates against the ephemeral file alone. At completion, `Reconcile` deterministically merges ISC checkmarks, Verification evidence, Decisions entries, and any new Changelog entries back to master, then archives the ephemeral file under `_ephemeral/.archive/`.

**Ephemeral files are derived views. They are never sources of truth. They are never hand-edited as policy. The master ISA is what persists.**

---

## Relationship to the Algorithm

The Algorithm at OBSERVE invokes this skill to scaffold or read an ISA. The skill does not run the Algorithm — it owns the artifact the Algorithm operates on.

- OBSERVE: `Skill("ISA", "scaffold from prompt at tier T")` → returns populated ISA at canonical location.
- OBSERVE: `Skill("ISA", "check completeness of <path> at tier T")` → pass/fail + gap report.
- PLAN: `Skill("ISA", "extract feature <name> as ephemeral file")` → ephemeral excerpt.
- LEARN: `Skill("ISA", "reconcile <ephemeral-path> → <master-path>")` → deterministic merge.

The Algorithm doctrine spec at `~/.claude/PAI/ALGORITHM/v6.2.0.md` (or LATEST) governs invocation cadence. This skill is invocation-agnostic — it works the same whether called by the Algorithm or directly by the user.

---

## Format spec cross-reference

The full ISA format spec lives at `~/.claude/PAI/DOCUMENTATION/IsaFormat.md`. This skill implements that spec; if there is ever a contradiction, the format spec wins and this skill is updated to match.

The system-architecture doc — five identities, three-guardrail taxonomy, twelve-section body, six workflows, two homes, subsystem relationships — lives at `~/.claude/PAI/DOCUMENTATION/Isa/IsaSystem.md`. Read that for the conceptual frame; read this file (and `IsaFormat.md`) for the operational contract.

- **Ephemeral files are derived views, never sources of truth.** Scaffold's `--ephemeral` mode produces a slice of the master ISA at `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/_ephemeral/<feature>.md`. Workers operate against that slice; Reconcile merges back. Hand-editing master content from an ephemeral file is policy-forbidden — the master is what persists; the ephemeral is what gets archived.

Append refuses to write a partial C/R/L; if any of the four is missing, the entry is a Decision, not a Changelog. ## Problem

LIMSOC Permission Assist is a single-page vanilla-JS tool (repo `nicholas-wood/limsoc-permission-assist`) that Life Saving Victoria uses to maintain LIMSOC permission groups. It runs only as a claude.ai artifact or a local file. It embeds a snapshot of LIMSOC staging group and permission names, so it cannot be put on a public URL, and it loads its Excel library from cdnjs, which rules out a strict content security policy. It has no home behind an organisational sign-in, no deploy pipeline, and no rollback.

## Vision

Nick opens `https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist`, signs in exactly as he does for the Operational Service Summary, and the page he knows appears with the staging example loaded. He uploads a Groups export, ticks, downloads the import file. Nothing about the tool changed; what changed is that a signed-out request gets the sign-in page and nothing else, the browser is technically unable to call anything but its own origin, and a push to main puts a new build live with the previous one a single command away.

## Out of Scope

- Any change to the app's behaviour, layout, wording or LIMSOC look beyond what hosting and security require.
- Any call to LIMSOC, production (limsoc.com.au) or staging, from the app, the gate, CI or my testing. Import testing on staging.limsoc.com.au is Nick's.
- A backend for group rules. They stay in localStorage (`lsvperm-rules`).
- A second sign-in system, load balancer, IAP, CDN, or a second Cloud Run service.
- Restructuring the Operational Service Summary app (its basePath, routes, or data model), which another session is still building.
- Analytics, error reporting or any third-party call.
- Making the repository public.

## Principles

- **One gate, one audit.** Sign-in, session and membership checks are the gate's existing code paths, not a copy.
- **Nothing readable without a session.** Page, vendored script, any other path under the prefix, and the bucket itself all refuse a signed-out request.
- **Least privilege by default.** A new app starts with one allowed person and an explicit grant per person after that.
- **The browser cannot be asked to misbehave.** The CSP forbids network calls outright, so "never talks to LIMSOC" is enforced, not promised.
- **Additive to shared things.** The gate repo and Terraform state are shared with in-flight work; changes there are new files or minimal hunks.
- **Cost honesty.** Anything outside the free tier is surfaced with an estimate before it is created.

## Constraints

- URL: `https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist`. The domain mapping is gated on Nick's GoDaddy nameserver change (inherited from the gate project); until then the interim host is `lsv-oss-prod-ixkidoqqka-ts.a.run.app`.
- Gate: Cloud Run service `lsv-oss-prod`, project `lsv-oss-prod`, australia-southeast1, Next.js 15.5.6 with `basePath: "/lsv/dailysummary"`, Firebase Auth session cookie `session` (httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Lax, 14 days), Firestore `members` allow-list.
- Storage: one GCS bucket in `lsv-oss-prod`, Standard class, australia-southeast1, uniform bucket-level access, public access prevention enforced, versioning on, no allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers, no signed URLs. Only `lsv-oss-run` holds `roles/storage.objectViewer` on it.
- CI: GitHub Actions with Workload Identity Federation, no JSON keys. Push to main builds and deploys.
- Build: edit `src/`, run `python3 build.py`, never hand-edit `dist/`. xlsx pinned at 0.18.5, vendored, hash-checked.

## Problem

LIMSOC Permission Assist is a single-page vanilla-JS tool (repo `nicholas-wood/limsoc-permission-assist`) that Life Saving Victoria uses to maintain LIMSOC permission groups. It runs only as a claude.ai artifact or a local file. It embeds a snapshot of LIMSOC staging group and permission names, so it cannot be put on a public URL, and it loads its Excel library from cdnjs, which rules out a strict content security policy. It has no home behind an organisational sign-in, no deploy pipeline, and no rollback.

## Vision

Nick opens `https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist`, signs in exactly as he does for the Operational Service Summary, and the page he knows appears with the staging example loaded. He uploads a Groups export, ticks, downloads the import file. Nothing about the tool changed; what changed is that a signed-out request gets the sign-in page and nothing else, the browser is technically unable to call anything but its own origin, and a push to main puts a new build live with the previous one a single command away.

## Out of Scope

- Any change to the app's behaviour, layout, wording or LIMSOC look beyond what hosting and security require.
- Any call to LIMSOC, production (limsoc.com.au) or staging, from the app, the gate, CI or my testing. Import testing on staging.limsoc.com.au is Nick's.
- A backend for group rules. They stay in localStorage (`lsvperm-rules`).
- A second sign-in system, load balancer, IAP, CDN, or a second Cloud Run service.
- Restructuring the Operational Service Summary app (its basePath, routes, or data model), which another session is still building.
- Analytics, error reporting or any third-party call.
- Making the repository public.

## Principles

- **One gate, one audit.** Sign-in, session and membership checks are the gate's existing code paths, not a copy.
- **Nothing readable without a session.** Page, vendored script, any other path under the prefix, and the bucket itself all refuse a signed-out request.
- **Least privilege by default.** A new app starts with one allowed person and an explicit grant per person after that.
- **The browser cannot be asked to misbehave.** The CSP forbids network calls outright, so "never talks to LIMSOC" is enforced, not promised.
- **Additive to shared things.** The gate repo and Terraform state are shared with in-flight work; changes there are new files or minimal hunks.
- **Cost honesty.** Anything outside the free tier is surfaced with an estimate before it is created.

## Constraints

- URL: `https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist`. The domain mapping is gated on Nick's GoDaddy nameserver change (inherited from the gate project); until then the interim host is `lsv-oss-prod-ixkidoqqka-ts.a.run.app`.
- Gate: Cloud Run service `lsv-oss-prod`, project `lsv-oss-prod`, australia-southeast1, Next.js 15.5.6 with `basePath: "/lsv/dailysummary"`, Firebase Auth session cookie `session` (httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Lax, 14 days), Firestore `members` allow-list.
- Storage: one GCS bucket in `lsv-oss-prod`, Standard class, australia-southeast1, uniform bucket-level access, public access prevention enforced, versioning on, no allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers, no signed URLs. Only `lsv-oss-run` holds `roles/storage.objectViewer` on it.
- CI: GitHub Actions with Workload Identity Federation, no JSON keys. Push to main builds and deploys.
- Build: edit `src/`, run `python3 build.py`, never hand-edit `dist/`. xlsx pinned at 0.18.5, vendored, hash-checked.
- Headers: strict CSP (`script-src 'self'` plus the inline script hash), `Cache-Control: no-store` on HTML, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, plus the gate's nosniff, frame deny, referrer, permissions and HSTS set.
- Tooling: bun and TypeScript for new scripts; Python only for the existing `build.py`. gcloud, terraform and gh exist only on the Mac (`ssh mac`).
- Wording: "members", never "staff".

LIMSOC Permission Assist is served at `/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist` by the existing `lsv-oss-prod` gate from a private versioned bucket, only to signed-in members holding an explicit grant (initially Nick alone), under a CSP that allows same-origin scripts and no network connections; a push to main of the app repo rebuilds and publishes it over WIF; and `DEPLOY.md` covers deploy, rollback, adding a member and monthly cost.

#!/usr/bin/env bun
/**
 * Writes test/groups-export-test.csv: a LIMSOC Groups export (columns name,
 * permissions) made from the staging snapshot, for checking upload and
 * download on the hosted page.
 *
 * It mirrors a real run the way the page's built-in example does: the
 * snapshot's Superuser list becomes "Superuser (last run)", and "Superuser"
 * holds every permission, as it would after Choose all. The difference is
 * what the page shows as new.
 *
 *   bun scripts/make-test-csv.ts
 */
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, resolve } from "node:path";

type Snapshot = { kind: string; perms: [number, string][]; groups: { name: string; perms: number[] }[] };

const root = resolve(dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname), "..");
const snap = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, "data/staging-snapshot-2026-11-14.json"), "utf8")) as Snapshot;
if (snap.kind !== "limsoc-permission-snapshot") throw new Error("Not a LIMSOC permission snapshot");

const codename = new Map(snap.perms.map(([id, label]) => [id, label.split(" | ").pop()!]));
const groups = snap.groups.map((g) => ({ name: g.name, perms: g.perms.map((id) => codename.get(id)!) }));
const superuser = groups.find((g) => /^superuser$/i.test(g.name));
if (!superuser) throw new Error("Snapshot has no Superuser group");
if (groups.some((g) => /^superuser\s*\(last run\)$/i.test(g.name))) throw new Error("Snapshot already has a last-run group");

const lastRun = { name: "Superuser (last run)", perms: [...superuser.perms] };
superuser.perms = [...new Set(codename.values())];
groups.push(lastRun);

const q = (s: string) => `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"`;
const rows = [["name", "permissions"], ...groups.map((g) => [g.name, g.perms.join(",")])];
const out = resolve(root, "test/groups-export-test.csv");
mkdirSync(dirname(out), { recursive: true });
writeFileSync(out, rows.map((r) => r.map(q).join(",")).join("\r\n") + "\r\n");

const before = new Set(lastRun.perms);
const fresh = superuser.perms.filter((p) => !before.has(p)).length;
console.log(`wrote ${out}: ${groups.length} groups, Superuser ${superuser.perms.length}, last run ${lastRun.perms.length}, new ${fresh}`);
EOF

import csv
rows=list(csv.reader(open('test/groups-export-test.csv',newline='')))

bad=[r[0] for r in rows[1:] if r[1] and all(x.strip().isdigit() for x in r[1].split(','))]; print('digit-only cells:',bad)
su=set(rows[[r[0] for r in rows].index('Superuser')][1].split(',')); lr=set(rows[[r[0] for r in rows].index('Superuser (last run)')][1].split(','))
print('last run subset of superuser:', lr<su, 'new:', len(su-lr)); print('max cell length', max(len(r[1]) for r in rows))
EOF
cat > .github/workflows/deploy.yml <<'EOF'
# Build on every push and pull request; publish to the private bucket on a
# push to main. Same shape as the AccessBuddy and LSV gate pipelines: GitHub
# OIDC to Google Cloud through Workload Identity Federation, no stored keys.
#
# The bucket is never public. The LSV gate (Cloud Run service lsv-oss-prod)
# reads it server-side for signed-in members. See DEPLOY.md.
name: Build and deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

env:
  GCP_PROJECT_ID: lsv-oss-prod
  BUCKET: lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist
  SITE_BASE: /lsv/limsoc-permission-assist/
  WIF_PROVIDER: projects/1081779282735/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github/providers/limsoc-permission-assist
  DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT: limsoc-pa-deploy@lsv-oss-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'deploy-production' || format('ci-{0}', github.ref) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build and check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14

      - name: Committed dist matches a fresh build
        run: |
          python3 build.py
          git diff --exit-code -- dist

      - name: Build for the hosted path
        run: python3 build.py

      - name: Check the built page
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The vendored library is the pinned xlsx 0.18.5 build.
          echo "c9506197caf809a075b6dee1da0d36fb19da7158ffe8a88e7b0c96c5d8623c99  dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js" | sha256sum -c -
          # Scripts load from this site only.
          grep -q '<script src="/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js"></script>' dist/index.html
          if grep -Eo '(src|href)="(https?:)?//[^"]*"' dist/index.html; then echo "external reference in built page"; exit 1; fi
          # The page never makes a network request of its own.
          if grep -En 'fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|WebSocket|sendBeacon|EventSource|importScripts' src/app.js; then echo "network call in app.js"; exit 1; fi
          if grep -n 'limsoc\.com\.au' src/app.js src/page.html; then echo "LIMSOC host referenced in src"; exit 1; fi

      - name: Test export generator
        run: |
          bun scripts/make-test-csv.ts
          git diff --exit-code -- test

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: site
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  deploy:
    name: Publish to the private bucket
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: [build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: site
          path: dist

      - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ env.WIF_PROVIDER }}
          service_account: ${{ env.DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      - name: Upload
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The library first, the page last, so the page never points at a file that is not there yet.
          gcloud storage cp dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js "gs://${BUCKET}/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js" \
            --content-type="text/javascript; charset=utf-8" --cache-control="private, no-cache" \
            --custom-metadata="commit=${GITHUB_SHA}"
          gcloud storage cp dist/index.html "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" \
            --content-type="text/html; charset=utf-8" --cache-control="private, no-store" \
            --custom-metadata="commit=${GITHUB_SHA}"

      - name: Verify what is live in the bucket
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test "$(gcloud storage cat "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$(sha256sum dist/index.html | cut -d' ' -f1)"
          gcloud storage ls -a "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" | tail -3
          gcloud storage objects describe "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" --format="value(generation,custom_fields.commit)"
EOF
git status --short

cat > .github/workflows/deploy.yml <<'EOF'
# Build on every push and pull request; publish to the private bucket on a
# push to main. Same shape as the AccessBuddy and LSV gate pipelines: GitHub
# OIDC to Google Cloud through Workload Identity Federation, no stored keys.
#
# The bucket is never public. The LSV gate (Cloud Run service lsv-oss-prod)
# reads it server-side for signed-in members. See DEPLOY.md.
name: Build and deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

env:
  GCP_PROJECT_ID: lsv-oss-prod
  BUCKET: lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist
  SITE_BASE: /lsv/limsoc-permission-assist/
  WIF_PROVIDER: projects/1081779282735/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github/providers/limsoc-permission-assist
  DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT: limsoc-pa-deploy@lsv-oss-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'deploy-production' || format('ci-{0}', github.ref) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build and check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14

      - name: Committed dist matches a fresh build
        run: |
          python3 build.py
          git diff --exit-code -- dist

      - name: Build for the hosted path
        run: python3 build.py

      - name: Check the built page
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The vendored library is the pinned xlsx 0.18.5 build.
          echo "c9506197caf809a075b6dee1da0d36fb19da7158ffe8a88e7b0c96c5d8623c99  dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js" | sha256sum -c -
          # Scripts load from this site only.
          grep -q '<script src="/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js"></script>' dist/index.html
          if grep -Eo '(src|href)="(https?:)?//[^"]*"' dist/index.html; then echo "external reference in built page"; exit 1; fi
          # The page never makes a network request of its own.
          if grep -En 'fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|WebSocket|sendBeacon|EventSource|importScripts' src/app.js; then echo "network call in app.js"; exit 1; fi
          if grep -n 'limsoc\.com\.au' src/app.js src/page.html; then echo "LIMSOC host referenced in src"; exit 1; fi

      - name: Test export generator
        run: |
          bun scripts/make-test-csv.ts
          git diff --exit-code -- test

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: site
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  deploy:
    name: Publish to the private bucket
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: [build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: site
          path: dist

      - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ env.WIF_PROVIDER }}
          service_account: ${{ env.DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      - name: Upload
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The library first, the page last, so the page never points at a file that is not there yet.
          gcloud storage cp dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js "gs://${BUCKET}/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js" \
            --content-type="text/javascript; charset=utf-8" --cache-control="private, no-cache" \
            --custom-metadata="commit=${GITHUB_SHA}"
          gcloud storage cp dist/index.html "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" \
            --content-type="text/html; charset=utf-8" --cache-control="private, no-store" \
            --custom-metadata="commit=${GITHUB_SHA}"

      - name: Verify what is live in the bucket
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test "$(gcloud storage cat "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$(sha256sum dist/index.html | cut -d' ' -f1)"
          gcloud storage ls -a "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" | tail -3
          gcloud storage objects describe "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" --format="value(generation,custom_fields.commit)"
EOF

# Deploying LIMSOC Permission Assist

Hosted at **https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist**, behind the same sign-in as the LSV Operational Service Summary.

## How it is put together

| Part | What | Where |
|------|------|-------|
| Site files | `index.html` and `vendor/xlsx.full.min.js` | Private bucket `gs://lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist` (project `lsv-oss-prod`, australia-southeast1, Standard class, versioned) |
| Gate | Cloud Run service `lsv-oss-prod`: checks the session, checks the member's grant, then reads the bucket server-side | Repo `nicholas-wood/lsv-service-summary` (`src/lib/static-app.ts`, `src/app/apps/[app]`) |
| Infrastructure | Bucket, IAM, deploy account, WIF provider | `infra/terraform/limsoc-permission-assist.tf` in the gate repo |
| Pipeline | Build and check on every push; publish on `main` | `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` in this repo |

The bucket has public access prevention enforced and uniform bucket-level access. No one can read it by URL, and no signed URLs are issued. Two accounts can touch it: the gate's runtime account (`lsv-oss-run`, read only) and this repo's deploy account (`limsoc-pa-deploy`, objects in this bucket only).

The page is served with a content security policy that allows scripts from this site only, plus the page's own inline script by hash, and allows no network connections at all (`connect-src 'none'`). The browser cannot call LIMSOC or anything else from this page. HTML is `no-store` and every response is `noindex`.

## Deploy

Push to `main`. GitHub Actions rebuilds with `SITE_BASE=/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist/`, checks the build, and uploads to the bucket. The gate picks up the new files on the next request; nothing is restarted.

```
git push origin main
```

Pull requests run the build and checks without publishing.

Make changes in `src/` and run `python3 build.py`; commit the rebuilt `dist/`. CI fails if `dist/` does not match a fresh build.

To publish by hand (needs `gcloud` signed in with access to the bucket):

```
SITE_BASE=/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist/ python3 build.py
B=gs://lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist
gcloud storage cp dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js $B/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js
gcloud storage cp dist/index.html $B/index.html
python3 build.py   # put dist/ back to the committed local-file build
```

## Rollback

Every upload keeps the previous build (the bucket keeps the ten most recent versions of each file). To put the previous page back:

```
B=gs://lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist
gcloud storage cp "$(gcloud storage ls -a $B/index.html | sort -t'#' -k2 -n | tail -2 | head -1)" $B/index.html
```

It is live on the next request. To pick a specific build, list them with `gcloud storage ls -a -l $B/index.html` and copy the one you want (`$B/index.html#<generation>`) over `$B/index.html`.

Then fix `main` (for example `git revert <commit> && git push`), or the next push will publish the same thing again.

## Adding a member

Access needs two things: the person is on the gate's member allow-list, and they hold the `limsoc-permission-assist` grant. One command does both. Run it from a checkout of the gate repo (`nicholas-wood/lsv-service-summary`) on a machine where `gcloud auth application-default login` has been done:

```
bun run scripts/app-access.ts grant limsoc-permission-assist person@example.com "First Last"
```

They then sign in at the address above with an emailed link. Other commands:

```
bun run scripts/app-access.ts list   limsoc-permission-assist
bun run scripts/app-access.ts revoke limsoc-permission-assist person@example.com
```

A grant or a revoke takes effect on the person's next request. Nothing is redeployed.

Note: the allow-list is shared with the Operational Service Summary. Anyone added here is a gate member, so today they can also open `/lsv/dailysummary`. Revoking the grant removes Permission Assist only; to remove someone entirely, remove them from the allow-list in the gate.

## Monthly cost

Effectively nothing: well under 5 cents a month.

| Item | Basis | Per month (USD) |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Storage | About 1.1 MB per build, up to 11 builds kept, Standard class at roughly $0.023 per GB | under $0.001 |
| Uploads | 2 writes per deploy at $0.005 per 1,000 | under $0.001 |
| Reads | 1 conditional read per page or script request at $0.0004 per 1,000 | under $0.001 |
| Network | Bucket to Cloud Run in the same region | $0 |
| Gate | Existing Cloud Run service, scales to zero, inside its free tier at this usage | $0 extra |

Regional buckets outside the US are not in Google Cloud's always-free allowance, so the storage line is a real charge, just a very small one.

## First-time setup (once)

1. Merge the gate change and apply its Terraform (`infra/terraform/limsoc-permission-assist.tf`), which creates the bucket, the read binding, the deploy account and the WIF provider.
2. Deploy the gate so the route exists.
3. Grant the first member (command above).
4. Create the `production` environment in this repo's GitHub settings, then push to `main`.

## Rules

- The app never calls LIMSOC. Import testing is done by hand on staging.limsoc.com.au only, never production.
- Keep this repository private. `data/` and `test/` describe LIMSOC's permission structure.
- Do not make the bucket public, add `allUsers`, or hand out signed URLs.

- SheetJS 0.18.5 is vendored in `vendor/` (sha256 pinned in `build.py`, identical to the cdnjs file) and loaded from beside the page instead of cdnjs.
- `SITE_BASE` sets the hosted path; unset keeps the local-file build working.
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: build and checks on every push and PR, publish to the private bucket on `main` through Workload Identity Federation (no keys).

- `DEPLOY.md`: deploy, rollback, adding a member, monthly cost.

cat > $T/pr-gate.md <<'EOF'
Serves LIMSOC Permission Assist (repo `nicholas-wood/limsoc-permission-assist`) at `/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist` through this gate, from a private bucket. Additive: no existing route, rule or Terraform resource changes.

**How**
- `next.config.ts`: the public path is outside the `/lsv/dailysummary` basePath, and Next only allows a rewrite from outside the basePath to an absolute URL, so it rewrites to this server over loopback (`/lsv/dailysummary/apps/<slug>`).
- `src/app/apps/[app]/[[...path]]/route.ts`: session first, then a per-app grant (`members/<email>.apps`), then the bucket read with the runtime account. Signed-out requests to any path get a 303 to sign-in.
- `src/lib/static-app.ts`: path allow-rules, CSP by hash (`script-src 'self' 'sha256-…'`, `connect-src 'none'`), no-store, noindex, conditional reads keyed on object generation.
- `src/middleware.ts`: `/apps/*` without a cookie redirects using the configured app URL (the loopback request has no public host).
- `scripts/app-access.ts`: grant, revoke, list.
- `infra/terraform/limsoc-permission-assist.tf`: bucket (Standard, single region, UBLA, public access prevention enforced, versioned), `objectViewer` for `lsv-oss-run` on that bucket only, deploy account `limsoc-pa-deploy` with `objectUser` on that bucket only, and its own WIF provider pinned to the app repo on `main`.

**Checked**
- 32 tests pass (16 new), typecheck clean, `next build` clean.
- Local production build: page, vendored script, unknown paths, traversal, tampered cookie and POST all return 303 to sign-in with no content.
- Headless Chrome against the same header code: example loads, csv upload, .xlsx and .csv downloads, zero CSP violations, requests to own origin only; a fetch to another host and an injected inline script are blocked.

**Not done yet (needs a go-ahead)**: `terraform apply`, first upload, grant, and deploying this revision. Signed-in checks against the live service follow that.

**Open point**: a grant requires gate membership, and membership currently also opens the Operational Service Summary.

# Deploying LIMSOC Permission Assist

Hosted at **https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist**, behind the same sign-in as the LSV Operational Service Summary.

## How it is put together

| Part | What | Where |
|------|------|-------|
| Site files | `index.html` and `vendor/xlsx.full.min.js` | Private bucket `gs://lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist` (project `lsv-oss-prod`, australia-southeast1, Standard class, versioned) |
| Gate | Cloud Run service `lsv-oss-prod`: checks the session, checks the member's grant, then reads the bucket server-side | Repo `nicholas-wood/lsv-service-summary` (`src/lib/static-app.ts`, `src/app/apps/[app]`) |
| Infrastructure | Bucket, IAM, deploy account, WIF provider | `infra/terraform/limsoc-permission-assist.tf` in the gate repo |
| Pipeline | Build and check on every push; publish on `main` | `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` in this repo |

The bucket has public access prevention enforced and uniform bucket-level access. No one can read it by URL, and no signed URLs are issued. Two accounts can touch it: the gate's runtime account (`lsv-oss-run`, read only) and this repo's deploy account (`limsoc-pa-deploy`, objects in this bucket only).

The page is served with a content security policy that allows scripts from this site only, plus the page's own inline script by hash, and allows no network connections at all (`connect-src 'none'`). The browser cannot call LIMSOC or anything else from this page. HTML is `no-store` and every response is `noindex`.

## Deploy

Push to `main`. GitHub Actions rebuilds with `SITE_BASE=/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist/`, checks the build, and uploads to the bucket. The gate picks up the new files on the next request; nothing is restarted.

```
git push origin main
```

Pull requests run the build and checks without publishing.

Make changes in `src/` and run `python3 build.py`; commit the rebuilt `dist/`. CI fails if `dist/` does not match a fresh build.

To publish by hand (needs `gcloud` signed in with access to the bucket):

```
SITE_BASE=/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist/ python3 build.py
B=gs://lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist
gcloud storage cp dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js $B/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js
gcloud storage cp dist/index.html $B/index.html
python3 build.py   # put dist/ back to the committed local-file build
```

## Rollback

Every upload keeps the previous build (the bucket keeps the ten most recent versions of each file). To put the previous page back:

```
B=gs://lsv-oss-prod-limsoc-permission-assist
gcloud storage cp "$(gcloud storage ls -a $B/index.html | sort -t'#' -k2 -n | tail -2 | head -1)" $B/index.html
```

It is live on the next request. To pick a specific build, list them with `gcloud storage ls -a -l $B/index.html` and copy the one you want (`$B/index.html#<generation>`) over `$B/index.html`.

Then fix `main` (for example `git revert <commit> && git push`), or the next push will publish the same thing again.

## Adding a member

Access needs two things: the person is on the gate's member allow-list, and they hold the `limsoc-permission-assist` grant. One command does both. Run it from a checkout of the gate repo (`nicholas-wood/lsv-service-summary`) on a machine where `gcloud auth application-default login` has been done:

```
bun run scripts/app-access.ts grant limsoc-permission-assist person@example.com "First Last"
```

They then sign in at the address above with an emailed link. Other commands:

```
bun run scripts/app-access.ts list   limsoc-permission-assist
bun run scripts/app-access.ts revoke limsoc-permission-assist person@example.com
```

A grant or a revoke takes effect on the person's next request. Nothing is redeployed.

Note: the allow-list is shared with the Operational Service Summary. Anyone added here is a gate member, so today they can also open `/lsv/dailysummary`. Revoking the grant removes Permission Assist only; to remove someone entirely, remove them from the allow-list in the gate.

## Monthly cost

Effectively nothing: well under 5 cents a month.

| Item | Basis | Per month (USD) |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Storage | About 1.1 MB per build, up to 11 builds kept, Standard class at roughly $0.023 per GB | under $0.001 |
| Uploads | 2 writes per deploy at $0.005 per 1,000 | under $0.001 |
| Reads | 1 conditional read per page or script request at $0.0004 per 1,000 | under $0.001 |
| Network | Bucket to Cloud Run in the same region | $0 |
| Gate | Existing Cloud Run service, scales to zero, inside its free tier at this usage | $0 extra |

Regional buckets outside the US are not in Google Cloud's always-free allowance, so the storage line is a real charge, just a very small one.

## First-time setup (once)

1. Merge the gate change and apply its Terraform (`infra/terraform/limsoc-permission-assist.tf`), which creates the bucket, the read binding, the deploy account and the WIF provider.
2. Deploy the gate so the route exists.
3. Grant the first member (command above).
4. Create the `production` environment in this repo's GitHub settings, then push to `main`.

## Rules

- The app never calls LIMSOC. Import testing is done by hand on staging.limsoc.com.au only, never production.
- Keep this repository private. `data/` and `test/` describe LIMSOC's permission structure.
- Do not make the bucket public, add `allUsers`, or hand out signed URLs.

content.content:
The attached ISA is for `budgetbuddy-phone-signin-unreachable`, not this task, so I reviewed only the design as you described it. Don't log this work against that ISA.

1. **Fatal if true: cookie Path.** Firebase session cookies set by a gate with basePath `/lsv/dailysummary` usually get `Path=/lsv/dailysummary`. The browser will then never send the cookie to `/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist`, which causes a sign-in redirect loop. Confirm the cookie is `Path=/` or `/lsv`, and that middleware's matcher actually fires on the public path, not just the loopback one.

2. **Loopback / Host check.** Host is client-controlled. That's harmless only if auth and the grant check run on every path, so that "via loopback" decides nothing but the 308. Make sure of that. Also check that no absolute URL is built from `req.url`/Host on the loopback leg, or you'll leak `http://127.0.0.1:8080/...` redirects to users. Use `$PORT` from the environment, never hardcode 8080.

3. **Possibly drop the loopback hop.** A `basePath:false` rewrite to an internal destination (`/lsv/dailysummary/apps/...`), or a middleware rewrite, may avoid the proxy hop entirely. That removes the Host heuristic and the extra request. Worth a 10-minute spike.

4. **Slug and key handling.** Allowlist the slug. Map it to a fixed object prefix server-side. Reject `..`, `%2e`, `%2f` and `\` after decoding. Check the grant against the normalized slug. The client path must never choose the bucket prefix.

5. **Biggest gap: same-origin trust.** Uploaded app JS runs on the gate's origin. A compromised app repo or CI could read same-origin IndexedDB/localStorage, including the Firebase JS SDK tokens if dailysummary uses them. It could exfiltrate via top-level navigation, which `connect-src 'none'` does not stop. Fix this with the CSP directive `sandbox allow-scripts allow-downloads` without `allow-same-origin`, which gives the app an opaque origin. Test that the app still works under it.

6. **CSP gaps.** `default-src` does not cover `frame-ancestors`, `base-uri`, `form-action` or `sandbox`. Add `frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`. Also send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, correct Content-Type on every asset, and `Vary: Cookie`.

7. **Blob downloads.** An `<a download href=blob:>` navigation is generally fine. Under `sandbox` you need `allow-downloads`, and some browsers also need `allow-popups` for `target=_blank`. `default-src 'none'` breaks any `img-src blob:` or `data:`, favicons and fonts, plus workers (`worker-src blob:`). `connect-src 'none'` breaks any `fetch()` of the app's own JSON or wasm. Grep the dist before go-live.

8. **CSP hash drift.** The sha256 must be computed by CI from the built `index.html` and served from metadata or a manifest, not pinned in gate code. Otherwise every rebuild silently breaks the app.

9. **Generation precondition.** Clarify where the generation comes from. If it's pinned in config, every upload needs a gate deploy. If it's read from live metadata, the precondition adds little. Either is fine, but decide deliberately.

10. **Auth hygiene.**
    - Use `verifySessionCookie(cookie, true)` so revoked sessions are rejected.
    - Lowercase the email before the `members/<email>` lookup.
    - Require `email_verified`.
    - Validate the sign-in `returnTo` against an allowlist so it can't become an open redirect.
    - Give the runtime SA `objectViewer` on this bucket only.

11. **WIF scoping.**
    - Put the attribute condition on the provider itself, not just the IAM binding.
    - Key it on `repository_id` and `repository_owner_id` rather than names, which are vulnerable to rename or takeover.
    - Bind `workloadIdentityUser` on that SA only.
    - `objectUser` includes overwrite and delete. Versioning covers recovery, but add branch protection or a GitHub environment with reviewers, since main is now code execution on your origin.

12. **Holding the deploy: yes, correct.** The GCS state lock prevents corruption but not stale plans, and the other session's deploy can roll back your revision or env vars. Sequence it like this:
    - Let them finish.
    - Rebase and run a fresh plan.
    - Never targeted-apply Cloud Run (same lesson as the AccessBuddy drift).
    - The bucket, WIF and IAM resources can go first if the plan shows zero Cloud Run diff.

📃 CONTENT:

**Nothing is live yet.** Everything is built, checked and sitting in two open PRs, but I stopped before creating any cloud resources or deploying. 23 of 74 criteria are verified; the rest need the deploy.

**Why I stopped**

- **Another session is deploying the same gate.** While I worked, the live `lsv-oss-prod` service went from revision 00004 to 00008 and `origin/main` moved twice. Deploying my image could roll their work back, and their next Terraform apply from a copy without my file would plan to destroy my resources.
- **You asked to be told before spend.** The bucket is technically outside the free tier (regional, non-US).
- **Two parts of the AccessBuddy approach did not fit**, and you asked me to check instead of inventing. Both are under "Decisions for you".

**What is ready**

- **App PR:** [limsoc-permission-assist#1](https://github.com/nicholas-wood/limsoc-permission-assist/pull/1), CI green.
  - xlsx 0.18.5 is vendored and hash-pinned; it is byte-identical to the cdnjs file.
  - `app.js` is untouched and `page.html` changes by one script tag.
  - It adds the deploy workflow (WIF, no keys), the test csv generator and `DEPLOY.md`.
- **Gate PR:** [lsv-service-summary#2](https://github.com/nicholas-wood/lsv-service-summary/pull/2), CI green, rebased onto the commit that was live when I checked.
  - A new route checks the session, then a per-app grant, then reads the bucket server-side.
  - Terraform adds the private versioned bucket, read access for `lsv-oss-run` on that bucket only, and a deploy account with its own WIF provider.
  - A read-only plan showed 7 resources to add and none destroyed.
- **Signed-out behaviour, local production build of the gate only:**

  | Request (no cookie) | Response |
  |---|---|
  | `GET /lsv/limsoc-permission-assist` | 303 to `/lsv/dailysummary/sign-in`, no body |
  | `GET …/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js` | 303 to sign-in, no body |
  | `GET …/a/b/c.html` and `…/..%2f..%2fapi/health` | 303 to sign-in |
  | Tampered `session` cookie, and `POST` | 303 to sign-in |

- **Browser behaviour, headless Chrome against the gate's header code (not the deployed site):**
  - The staging example loads.
  - The test csv uploads (29 groups in the file, 59 new permissions).
  - Download .xlsx and Download .csv both work.
  - There were zero CSP violations, and requests went to the page's own origin only.
  - The CSP is `script-src 'self'` plus one hash, with `connect-src 'none'`, so the page cannot call LIMSOC or anything else.

**Not yet checked**

- Nothing signed-in has run against the real service, and the bucket refusal can't be shown until the bucket exists.
- My last Terraform edit (pinning the WIF provider to GitHub's numeric repo IDs) is pushed but has not been through `terraform validate`; the Mac dropped off SSH.
- The Interceptor pass in your Chrome is owed after go-live.

**Cost**

Well under 5 US cents a month: about 1.1 MB per build with up to 11 versions kept, and no new Cloud Run service.

**Decisions for you**

1. **Routing.** The gate's Next.js `basePath` is `/lsv/dailysummary`, so it cannot answer `/lsv/limsoc-permission-assist` directly. I used a rewrite that sends that path to the gate itself over loopback; Next rejects the simpler internal rewrite at build time. The alternative is changing the base path to `/lsv` and moving every dailysummary route, which I avoided while that app is mid-build.
2. **Access model.** Access is a per-app grant on the existing `members` allow-list. The catch is that anyone granted is also a gate member, which today also opens `/lsv/dailysummary`. Say so if you want Permission Assist-only people and I will add a matching check on the dailysummary side.
3. **Shared origin.** The page shares a browser origin with the Operational Service Summary. A CSP `sandbox` would isolate it but break the localStorage group rules you asked to keep, so I left it out.

**Go-live, once you say go and the other session is paused**

1. Merge gate PR #2 and apply the seven new resources from the shared Terraform copy.
2. Deploy the gate.

# Checks for both halves of the repo: the page (src/, build.py) and the host
# service that serves it behind sign-in (host/). Runs on pull requests and is
# called by the publish and deploy workflows.
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_call:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  site:
    name: Page - build and check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14

      - name: Committed dist matches a fresh build
        run: |
          python3 build.py
          git diff --exit-code -- dist

      - name: Build for hosting at the site root
        env:
          SITE_BASE: /
        run: python3 build.py

      - name: Check the built page
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The vendored library is the pinned xlsx 0.18.5 build.
          echo "c9506197caf809a075b6dee1da0d36fb19da7158ffe8a88e7b0c96c5d8623c99  dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js" | sha256sum -c -
          # Scripts load from this site only.
          grep -q '<script src="/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js"></script>' dist/index.html
          if grep -Eo '(src|href)="(https?:)?//[^"]*"' dist/index.html; then echo "external reference in built page"; exit 1; fi
          # The page never makes a network request of its own.
          if grep -En 'fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|WebSocket|sendBeacon|EventSource|importScripts' src/app.js; then echo "network call in app.js"; exit 1; fi
          if grep -n 'limsoc\.com\.au' src/app.js src/page.html; then echo "LIMSOC host referenced in src"; exit 1; fi

      - name: Test export generator is current
        run: |
          bun scripts/make-test-csv.ts
          git diff --exit-code -- test

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: site
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  host:
    name: Host - lint, type check, test, build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: host
    env:
      NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL: https://permissions.nicholaswood.com.au
      NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID: limsoc-pa-prod
      NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN: limsoc-pa-prod.firebaseapp.com
      NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY: ci-placeholder
      NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID: ci-placeholder
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run lint
      - run: bun run typecheck
      - run: bun run test
      - run: bun run build

cat > .github/workflows/site.yml <<'EOF'
# A push to main rebuilds the page and publishes it to the private bucket.
# GitHub OIDC to Google Cloud through Workload Identity Federation, no stored
# keys. The bucket is never public: the host service reads it server-side for
# signed-in members, and picks up a new upload on the next request.
name: Publish site

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

env:
  BUCKET: limsoc-pa-prod-site
  WIF_PROVIDER: __WIF_PROVIDER__
  DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT: limsoc-pa-deploy@limsoc-pa-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com

concurrency:
  group: publish-site
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  ci:
    name: CI
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  publish:
    name: Publish to the private bucket
    needs: [ci]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: site
          path: dist

      - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ env.WIF_PROVIDER }}
          service_account: ${{ env.DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      - name: Upload
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The library first, the page last, so the page never points at a file that is not there yet.
          gcloud storage cp dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js "gs://${BUCKET}/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js" \
            --content-type="text/javascript; charset=utf-8" --cache-control="private, no-cache" \
            --custom-metadata="commit=${GITHUB_SHA}"
          gcloud storage cp dist/index.html "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" \
            --content-type="text/html; charset=utf-8" --cache-control="private, no-store" \
            --custom-metadata="commit=${GITHUB_SHA}"

      - name: Verify what is live in the bucket
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test "$(gcloud storage cat "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$(sha256sum dist/index.html | cut -d' ' -f1)"
          gcloud storage ls -a "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" | tail -3
          gcloud storage objects describe "gs://${BUCKET}/index.html" --format="value(generation,custom_fields.commit)"
EOF
cat > .github/workflows/release-please.yml <<'EOF'
# Same release flow as AccessBuddy: release-please keeps a release PR open;
# merging it cuts a release, and the release deploys the host service.
# (The page itself publishes on every push to main: see site.yml.)
name: Release Please

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  release-please:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      release_created: ${{ steps.release.outputs.release_created }}
      version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: googleapis/release-please-action@v4
        id: release

  deploy:
    name: Deploy
    needs: [release-please]
    if: ${{ needs.release-please.outputs.release_created == 'true' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/deploy.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ needs.release-please.outputs.version }}
    secrets: inherit
EOF
cat > .github/workflows/deploy.yml <<'EOF'
# Called by release-please when a release is created. Same shape as
# AccessBuddy's deploy.yml: WIF auth, build, push, update the Cloud Run
# service to the sha image, check the live version.
name: Deploy host

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      version:
        required: true
        type: string

env:
  GCP_PROJECT_ID: limsoc-pa-prod
  GCP_REGION: australia-southeast1
  CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE: limsoc-pa-prod
  AR_REPO: limsoc-pa
  IMAGE_NAME: host
  APP_URL: __APP_URL__
  WIF_PROVIDER: __WIF_PROVIDER__
  DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT: limsoc-pa-deploy@limsoc-pa-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  # Firebase web config: public identifiers, not secrets.
  FIREBASE_API_KEY: __FIREBASE_API_KEY__
  FIREBASE_APP_ID: "__FIREBASE_APP_ID__"

concurrency:
  group: deploy-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  ci:
    name: CI
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to Cloud Run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [ci]
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ env.WIF_PROVIDER }}
          service_account: ${{ env.DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      - run: gcloud auth configure-docker ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev --quiet

      - name: Build image
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=${{ env.APP_URL }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=${{ env.FIREBASE_API_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}.firebaseapp.com \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=${{ env.FIREBASE_APP_ID }} \
            --build-arg APP_VERSION=${{ inputs.version }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:v${{ inputs.version }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:latest host

      - name: Push image
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          docker push ${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }}
          docker push ${IMAGE}:v${{ inputs.version }}
          docker push ${IMAGE}:latest

      - name: Deploy to Cloud Run
        run: |
          gcloud run services update ${{ env.CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE }} \
            --image=${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --region=${{ env.GCP_REGION }} \
            --project=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}

      - name: Verify deployed version
        run: |
          sleep 10
          curl -fsS ${{ env.APP_URL }}/api/health | tee /dev/stderr | grep -q '"version":"${{ inputs.version }}"'
EOF

{
  "packages": {
    ".": {
      "release-type": "simple",
      "version-file": "VERSION"
    }
  }
}
EOF

cat > host/cloudbuild.yaml <<'EOF'
# One-off image build on Cloud Build (free tier: 120 build-minutes a day), for
# the first deploy or when GitHub Actions is unavailable. Normal deploys go
# through .github/workflows/deploy.yml. From host/:
#   gcloud builds submit --config cloudbuild.yaml --project limsoc-pa-prod \
#     --substitutions=_TAG=manual-1,_APP_URL=https://...,_API_KEY=...,_APP_ID=...,_VERSION=0.1.0
steps:
  - name: gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker
    args:
      - build
      - --build-arg=NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=${_APP_URL}
      - --build-arg=NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=${_API_KEY}
      - --build-arg=NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=limsoc-pa-prod.firebaseapp.com
      - --build-arg=NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=limsoc-pa-prod
      - --build-arg=NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=${_APP_ID}
      - --build-arg=APP_VERSION=${_VERSION}
      - -t
      - australia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/limsoc-pa-prod/limsoc-pa/host:${_TAG}
      - .
images:
  - australia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/limsoc-pa-prod/limsoc-pa/host:${_TAG}
options:
  logging: CLOUD_LOGGING_ONLY
substitutions:
  _TAG: manual
  _APP_URL: https://limsoc-pa-prod.web.app
  _API_KEY: ""
  _APP_ID: ""
  _VERSION: "0.1.0"
EOF

  WIF_PROVIDER: __WIF_PROVIDER__
  DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT: limsoc-pa-deploy@limsoc-pa-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  # Firebase web config: public identifiers, not secrets.
  FIREBASE_API_KEY: __FIREBASE_API_KEY__
  FIREBASE_APP_ID: "__FIREBASE_APP_ID__"

concurrency:
  group: deploy-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  ci:
    name: CI
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to Cloud Run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [ci]
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ env.WIF_PROVIDER }}
          service_account: ${{ env.DEPLOY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      - run: gcloud auth configure-docker ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev --quiet

      - name: Build image
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=${{ env.APP_URL }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=${{ env.FIREBASE_API_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}.firebaseapp.com \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=${{ env.FIREBASE_APP_ID }} \
            --build-arg APP_VERSION=${{ inputs.version }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:v${{ inputs.version }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:latest host

      - name: Push image
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          docker push ${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }}
          docker push ${IMAGE}:v${{ inputs.version }}
          docker push ${IMAGE}:latest

      - name: Deploy to Cloud Run
        run: |
          gcloud run services update ${{ env.CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE }} \
            --image=${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --region=${{ env.GCP_REGION }} \
            --project=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}

      - name: Verify deployed version
        run: |
          sleep 10
          curl -fsS ${{ env.APP_URL }}/api/health | tee /dev/stderr | grep -q '"version":"${{ inputs.version }}"'
EOF

      - --build-arg=APP_VERSION=${_VERSION}
      - -t
      - australia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/limsoc-pa-prod/limsoc-pa/host:${_TAG}

images:

input.content:
# Deploying LIMSOC Permission Assist

Hosted on its own, behind its own sign-in. It follows the AccessBuddy and LSV Operational Service Summary patterns but shares nothing with either.

- Address: **https://permissions.nicholaswood.com.au** (once the DNS record below exists). Until then: **https://limsoc-pa-prod.web.app**.
- Google Cloud project: `limsoc-pa-prod`, region australia-southeast1.

## How it is put together

| Part | What | Where |
|------|------|-------|
| The page | `index.html` and `vendor/xlsx.full.min.js`, built by `build.py` | Private bucket `gs://limsoc-pa-prod-site` (Standard class, single region, versioned) |
| Host service | Cloud Run service `limsoc-pa-prod`: sign-in, session, member allow-list, then reads the bucket server-side | `host/` (Next.js, sign-in code ported from AccessBuddy by way of the Service Summary) |
| Sign-in | Firebase Auth emailed link; 14-day httpOnly `__session` cookie; allow-list in Firestore `members/` | project `limsoc-pa-prod` |
| Front door | Firebase Hosting site `limsoc-pa-prod`, every path rewritten to the Cloud Run service (Cloud Run domain mappings are not offered in australia-southeast1) | `infra/terraform/main.tf` |
| Infrastructure | All of the above, plus secrets, service accounts and the GitHub trust | `infra/terraform` (state in `gs://limsoc-pa-prod-tfstate`) |
| Pipelines | `site.yml` publishes the page on every push to `main`; `release-please.yml` and `deploy.yml` release the host service | `.github/workflows` |

The bucket has public access prevention enforced and uniform bucket-level access. No one can read it by URL and no signed URLs are issued. Two accounts can touch it: the service's runtime account (`limsoc-pa-run`, read only) and the GitHub deploy account (`limsoc-pa-deploy`, objects in this bucket only).

The page is served with a content security policy that allows scripts from this site only, plus the page's own inline script by hash, and allows no network connections at all (`connect-src 'none'`). The browser cannot call LIMSOC or anything else from this page. HTML is `no-store` and every response is `noindex`.

## Deploy

**The page.** Push to `main`. GitHub Actions rebuilds it, checks it, and uploads it to the bucket. The service picks up the new files on the next request; nothing is restarted.

```
git push origin main
```

Make changes in `src/` and run `python3 build.py`; commit the rebuilt `dist/`. CI fails if `dist/` does not match a fresh build. Pull requests run the checks without publishing.

**The host service** (`host/`, rarely changes). Merge the open "release" pull request that release-please maintains. That cuts a release, builds the image and updates Cloud Run.

To publish the page by hand (needs `gcloud` signed in with access to the bucket):

```
SITE_BASE=/ python3 build.py
B=gs://limsoc-pa-prod-site
gcloud storage cp dist/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js $B/vendor/xlsx.full.min.js
gcloud storage cp dist/index.html $B/index.html
python3 build.py   # put dist/ back to the committed local-file build
```

## Rollback

**The page.** Every upload keeps the previous build (the bucket keeps the ten most recent versions of each file). To put the previous page back:

```
B=gs://limsoc-pa-prod-site
gcloud storage cp "$(gcloud storage ls -a $B/index.html | sort -t'#' -k2 -n | tail -2 | head -1)" $B/index.html
```

It is live on the next request. To pick a specific build, list them with `gcloud storage ls -a -l $B/index.html` and copy the one you want (`$B/index.html#<generation>`) over `$B/index.html`. Then fix `main` (for example `git revert <commit> && git push`), or the next push will publish the same thing again.

**The host service.** Send traffic back to the previous revision:

```
gcloud run revisions list --service limsoc-pa-prod --region australia-southeast1 --project limsoc-pa-prod --limit 3
gcloud run services update-traffic limsoc-pa-prod --to-revisions <previous-revision>=100 --region australia-southeast1 --project limsoc-pa-prod
```

## Adding a member

Only people on the allow-list can sign in. From `host/`, on a machine where `gcloud auth application-default login` has been done:

```
bun run members add person@example.com "First Last"
```

They then go to the address above, enter their email, and use the link they are sent. Other commands:

```
bun run members list
bun run members remove person@example.com
bun run members add person@example.com "First Last" --admin   # may also manage members through /api/members
```

Adding takes effect at the person's next sign-in. Removing takes effect on their next request and ends their sessions. Nothing is redeployed.

## Monthly cost

Cents: under 50 US cents a month at the outside, most likely under 10.

| Item | Basis | Per month (USD) |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Page storage | About 1.1 MB per build, up to 11 builds kept, Standard class at roughly $0.023 per GB | under $0.001 |
| Bucket operations | 2 writes per publish; 1 conditional read per page or script request | under $0.001 |
| Container images | Artifact Registry keeps the 3 newest images; 0.5 GB is free, then $0.10 per GB | $0 to about $0.10 |
| Cloud Run | Scales to zero; free tier is 2 million requests and 180,000 vCPU-seconds a month | $0 at this usage |
| Firestore, Firebase sign-in, Firebase Hosting, Secret Manager (1 secret), Cloud Build (first deploy only) | Inside their free tiers at this usage | $0 |
| Network | Bucket to Cloud Run in the same region | $0 |

Regional buckets outside the US are not in Google Cloud's always-free allowance, so the storage line is a real charge, just a very small one.

## The custom domain

Firebase Hosting needs DNS records at GoDaddy for `permissions.nicholaswood.com.au`. To see exactly which:

```
cd infra/terraform && terraform output custom_domain_dns_records
```

Add them at GoDaddy. When `terraform output custom_domain_state` shows the host active and the certificate issued, set `serve_on_domain = true` in `prod.tfvars`, `terraform apply`, update `APP_URL` in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` to the custom address, and release the host service so its links use it.

## Checking a deployment

`host/scripts/probe.ts` exercises the live service without needing the email: signed-out refusals for the page, the script and the bucket, then a real session for a member and the signed-in responses and headers.

```
cd host
APP_URL=https://limsoc-pa-prod.web.app NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=<terraform output firebase_api_key> bun run probe you@example.com
```

## First-time setup (already done; recorded for rebuilds)

```
gcloud projects create limsoc-pa-prod --name="LIMSOC Permission Assist"
gcloud billing projects link limsoc-pa-prod --billing-account=<account>
gcloud storage buckets create gs://limsoc-pa-prod-tfstate --project limsoc-pa-prod --location=australia-southeast1 --uniform-bucket-level-access --public-access-prevention
gcloud storage buckets update gs://limsoc-pa-prod-tfstate --versioning
cd infra/terraform && cp example.tfvars prod.tfvars
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=limsoc-pa-prod-tfstate" && terraform apply -var-file=prod.tfvars
```

Then build and deploy the first image (`host/cloudbuild.yaml`), publish the page, add the first member, and in GitHub create the `production` environment and allow Actions to create pull requests (for release-please).

## Rules

- The app never calls LIMSOC. Import testing is done by hand on staging.limsoc.com.au only, never production.
- Keep this repository private. `data/` and `test/` describe LIMSOC's permission structure.
- Do not make the bucket public, add `allUsers` to it, or hand out signed URLs.

Note: the allow-list is shared with the Operational Service Summary. Anyone added here is a gate member, so today they can also open `/lsv/dailysummary`. Revoking the grant removes Permission Assist only; to remove someone entirely, remove them from the allow-list in the gate.

## Monthly cost

Effectively nothing: well under 5 cents a month.

| Item | Basis | Per month (USD) |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| Storage | About 1.1 MB per build, up to 11 builds kept, Standard class at roughly $0.023 per GB | under $0.001 |
| Uploads | 2 writes per deploy at $0.005 per 1,000 | under $0.001 |
| Reads | 1 conditional read per page or script request at $0.0004 per 1,000 | under $0.001 |
| Network | Bucket to Cloud Run in the same region | $0 |
| Gate | Existing Cloud Run service, scales to zero, inside its free tier at this usage | $0 extra |

Regional buckets outside the US are not in Google Cloud's always-free allowance, so the storage line is a real charge, just a very small one.

## First-time setup (once)

1. Merge the gate change and apply its Terraform (`infra/terraform/limsoc-permission-assist.tf`), which creates the bucket, the read binding, the deploy account and the WIF provider.
2. Deploy the gate so the route exists.
3. Grant the first member (command above).
4. Create the `production` environment in this repo's GitHub settings, then push to `main`.

## Rules

- The app never calls LIMSOC. Import testing is done by hand on staging.limsoc.com.au only, never production.
- Keep this repository private. `data/` and `test/` describe LIMSOC's permission structure.
- Do not make the bucket public, add `allUsers`, or hand out signed URLs.
